title: The Empty Inheritance
premise: When a stranger's corpse is found in the flooded quarry wearing clothes stolen from her own closet, Theo Eastwick — the Grand Meridian Hotel's concierge and the town's unofficial keeper of secrets — realizes the dead man was dressed to be mistaken for her. The murder reopens the twenty-year-old disappearance of hotel heiress Cordelia Vane, a case Theo helped quietly bury when she was a young desk clerk who saw too much. As she follows a trail of misfiled ledgers, forged signatures, and a loyalty oath sworn by four employees on the night Cordelia vanished, Theo discovers the inheritance everyone fought over was never money at all but Cordelia's evidence of the town's laundering operation. The killer is Edmund Hale, the beloved retired manager who protected Theo all these years precisely because her silence was his alibi; in the end Theo chooses truth over the loyalty that sheltered her, trading her own safety for Cordelia's posthumous vindication as the quarry gives up its last secret.
about_author: Wren Marchetti spent a decade working front desks in grand old hotels before turning to crime fiction, collecting the small human dramas of lobbies and late shifts along the way. She lives in a converted bellhop quarters with an aging cat named Concierge.

chapters.title: The Register
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A routine night shift at the Grand Meridian: Theo checks in a nervous guest, notices his scuffed shoes don't match his expensive suit, and files the detail away. Establishes her gift for observation and her meticulous mental archive of the town's secrets. Emotional beat: quiet pride in being indispensable and invisible.

chapters.title: Clothes That Weren't Hers
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Police wake her at dawn: a body in the quarry, dressed in her gray wool coat and monogrammed scarf. Detective Imara Sable questions her; the clothes are unmistakably from Theo's closet, yet nothing was stolen. Beat: cold fear — someone wanted the dead man to be her.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, with a flashback. The victim is identified as a private investigator named Rook. Theo recalls, reluctantly, the night in 2004 when heiress Cordelia Vane disappeared and four hotel employees swore an oath of silence — Theo among them. Beat: guilt resurfacing like water rising.

chapters.title: The Fourth Floor Is Sealed
chapters.summary: Detective Sable's POV. Sable works the case officially while privately distrusting the hotel's spotless records. She finds Rook had booked room 412 — the sealed Vane suite — under a false name. Beat: professional suspicion sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: Alphabetized Secrets
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Searching her own memory archive, Theo reconstructs what Rook must have been investigating: the Vane estate, the will, the missing month of ledgers. Someone ransacked her apartment while she was at the police station. Beat: violation; the hunter knows where she lives.

chapters.title: Edmund Hale's Kindness
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Retired manager Edmund Hale, her old mentor, brings her soup and gentle warnings to stop digging. His warmth is genuine — and so is the chill Theo feels when he mentions the oath unprompted. Beat: love shadowed by dread.

chapters.title: What the Quarry Keeps
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Divers recover Rook's briefcase from the quarry: empty, but lined with paper impressions matching pages torn from a 2004 ledger. Sable begins pulling the old Vane file and finds it suspiciously thin. Beat: the past has been edited.

chapters.title: The Oath
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo tracks down the other three oath-keepers: bartender Delia, now dying; accountant Moss, now wealthy; and porter Ansel, who fled town years ago. Delia, lucid for an hour, tells her: 'We didn't hide a body, girl. We hid a ledger.' Beat: the case cracks open.

chapters.title: Room 412
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Using a master key she should have surrendered, Theo enters the sealed Vane suite and finds it preserved like a shrine — and recently disturbed. In the writing desk's false back: a photograph of Cordelia alive, dated six months after her disappearance. Beat: vertigo; everything is wrong.

chapters.title: A Witness Recants
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable interviews Moss, whose alibi from 2004 collapses under one careful question. He lawyers up within minutes. Meanwhile an anonymous note arrives at the station: 'Ask the concierge what she filed.' Beat: pressure converging on Theo from both sides.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo confronts why she stayed silent twenty years ago: Hale covered up her own small theft as a desperate young clerk, binding her loyalty forever. She understands now how debts become cages. Beat: painful self-recognition; she was bought cheaply and kept long.

chapters.title: Ansel Comes Home
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Ansel returns to town, terrified, claiming Rook contacted him first. Before Theo can get the full story, Ansel's car goes off the road — brakes tampered. He survives barely, whispering: 'Hale didn't do it alone.' Beat: grief and urgency; the clock starts.

chapters.title: Two Sets of Books
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable and Theo form an uneasy alliance. Reconstructing the missing ledger month, they find the hotel laundered money through phantom guests — and Cordelia discovered it. Her 'inheritance' was the evidence itself. Beat: revelation reframing the whole mystery.

chapters.title: The Second Signature
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The forged signatures on the estate settlement include one belonging to someone too young to have signed legally: Cordelia's cousin Julian Vane, now the estate's trustee and the hotel's silent owner. Julian denies everything elegantly. Beat: a new suspect, polished and plausible.

chapters.title: Delia's Last Hour
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Delia dies, but not before pressing a key into Theo's hand — an old locker key from the bus station, tagged 'C.V.' Theo retrieves a bundle: Cordelia's letters, proving she lived in hiding and feared 'the man who signs for me.' Beat: mourning braided with hope.

chapters.title: Mistaken for the Dead
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Forensics finally identifies how Rook was meant to pass as Theo: the killer studied her routines for months, using staff schedules only management could access. Sable narrows the list to two names. Beat: the noose tightening around the hotel's inner circle.

chapters.title: The Trap in the Lobby
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo proposes baiting the killer with a fake ledger page announcing itself in tonight's mail. She plays her old role — observant, invisible — watching every face in the lobby as the news lands. One guest's reaction betrays him: Julian's fixer. Beat: tension at its highest pitch; the hunt reverses.

chapters.title: Hale Confesses Everything
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Confronted, Hale breaks: he ran the laundering scheme, Cordelia found out, and he helped her vanish to save her life — then spent twenty years protecting that secret, killing Rook only when Rook threatened to expose Cordelia as alive and destroy the estate settlement. Beat: devastating; her protector was her captor of sorts all along.

chapters.title: Where Cordelia Went
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Following Hale's confession and the letters, Sable traces Cordelia to a coastal town — where she died peacefully two winters ago, leaving a sealed statement naming every signature she was forced to forge. Beat: bittersweet closure; justice arriving too late to matter to the one who earned it.

chapters.title: Julian's Last Check-In
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Julian, exposed, attempts to flee through the hotel he secretly owns — and Theo, knowing every corridor, shortcut, and service elevator, corners him herself in the sealed fourth floor. Sable makes the arrest. Beat: triumphant catharsis; the invisible woman becomes the visible hand of justice.

chapters.title: Settling Accounts
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Hale, ill and broken, accepts arrest and tells Theo her silence was the one debt he never should have collected. The Vane estate is unwound; Cordelia's true will surfaces, leaving a modest bequest 'to the clerk who saw me leave.' Beat: grief, gratitude, and release.

chapters.title: The Empty Inheritance
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, epilogue. Months later, Theo declines promotion to manager and instead opens the hotel's archives to the town, alphabetizing truth instead of secrets. Room 412 becomes a memorial. On the register's first line, she writes her own name at last. Beat: peace earned; loyalty finally aligned with truth.
